name: rush-type
title: Rush Type
description: White words blast into vertical RGB shutter trails, one forceful word at a time: the word falls out of perspective, stretches into a tall red/green/blue-fringed smear, snaps to a sharp readable rest, then blasts away as the next word arrives. The fringing comes from motion alone, not from tinting the text; a tube mask and glow ride along with the blast. WebGL, over an opaque background colour.
useWhen: A short phrase should cycle one forceful word at a time.
Chromatic separation should emerge from motion rather than tinting the text.
A kinetic-type beat needs a sharp readable rest between extreme blasts.
avoidWhen: The text must remain readable throughout the motion: use word-push or zoom-words.
You want a horizontal digital glitch: use rgb-glitch-text.
The block must remain transparent: it always paints an opaque background.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Phrase
variables.description: A short phrase; one whitespace-separated word is shown per cycle (up to 8 words).

variables.label: Resting size
variables.description: Cap height of the resting word, in pixels of a 1280×720 frame; scales with the frame.

variables.label: Vertical stretch
variables.description: Authored vertical scale at the blast, before perspective.

variables.label: Chromatic spread
variables.description: 0 removes the red/green/blue separation, 1 is the reference look, 2 exaggerates it.

variables.label: Rest duration
variables.description: Frames a word rests, readable (30 per second).

variables.label: Peak hold
variables.description: Total frames the blast hangs near the point around the word swap.

variables.label: Speed
variables.description: Playback multiplier for the whole motion.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Thin shutter trails and the tube mask look the same at 0.75 as at 1.
